title: XIV. Received opinion: Old-Testament faithful not received into paradise until Christ opened it; limbus patrum
pass_a_gloss: He descended, it says, toward the inferi, that he might rescue the saints who stood as held there — which sentence clearly also assert Irenaeus, Tertullian, Origen, Gregory of Neocaesarea, Eusebius, Macarius of Jerusalem, Basil, Athanasius, Epiphanius, Cyril of Jerusalem, Ambrose, Rufinus, Synesius, and even among the juniors Zwingli on Hebrews 11:39–40, Calvin in the Psychopannychia, Bullinger on Luke 16:23 and Hebrews 9:8 and 1 Peter 3:19, and Martyr on 2 Kings 2:13. So John Chrysostom (homily 4 on Mark), Jerome to Heliodorus in the epitaph of Nepotianus, likewise to Paula on the death of Blesilla and on Ecclesiastes chapters 3 and 9, Augustine (City of God book 20, chapter 15, and letter 99 to Evodius), the Council of Toledo under Honorius celebrated in the year 633 (chapter 1): In these things also, he says, that he sees Abraham among the infernal, this reason stands as thought by some to underlie, that all the saints before the advent belonging toward the Lord Jesus Christ stand as said to have descended even toward the inferi, though into a place of refreshment. Theophilus of Antioch among the ancients (Allegories book 4): But this stands as among those questions on account of which the Church ought least to stand as troubled or split, as Calvin authorizes (Institutes book 4, chapter 1, §12) — especially if there stands as consensus in this, that the souls belonging toward the ancient fathers immediately from their departure obtained beatitude and the beneficent presence of God. The positive and received sentence belonging toward the ancients down to our Sardian age stood as that the souls belonging toward the faithful belonging toward the Old Testament stood as not received into paradise before Christ by his death had unlocked it and first entered it with the thief. XIV.
pass_b_english: XIV. The positive and received sentence of the ancients down to our Sardian age was that the souls of the faithful of the Old Testament were not received into paradise before Christ by his death had unlocked it and first entered it with the thief. But this is among those questions on account of which the Church ought least to be troubled or split, as Calvin authorizes (Institutes book 4, chapter 1, §12) — especially if there is consensus in this, that the souls of the ancient fathers immediately from their departure obtained beatitude and the beneficent presence of God. Theophilus of Antioch among the ancients (Allegories book 4): In these things also, he says, that he sees Abraham among the infernal, this reason is thought by some to underlie, that all the saints before the advent of the Lord Jesus Christ are said to have descended even to the inferi, though into a place of refreshment.

So John Chrysostom (homily 4 on Mark), Jerome to Heliodorus in the epitaph of Nepotianus, likewise to Paula on the death of Blesilla and on Ecclesiastes chapters 3 and 9, Augustine (City of God book 20, chapter 15, and letter 99 to Evodius), the Council of Toledo under Honorius celebrated in the year 633 (chapter 1): He descended, it says, to the inferi, that he might rescue the saints who were held there — which sentence clearly also assert Irenaeus, Tertullian, Origen, Gregory of Neocaesarea, Eusebius, Macarius of Jerusalem, Basil, Athanasius, Epiphanius, Cyril of Jerusalem, Ambrose, Rufinus, Synesius, and even among the juniors Zwingli on Hebrews 11:39–40, Calvin in the Psychopannychia, Bullinger on Luke 16:23 and Hebrews 9:8 and 1 Peter 3:19, and Martyr on 2 Kings 2:13.
source_text: XIV. Positiva receptaque veterum ad nostrum usque Sardeniense saeculum sententia fuit, animas fidelium veteris testamenti non prius in paradisum fuisse receptas, quam cum morte sua reserasset Christus, primusque illum cum latrone esset ingressus. Haec vero est inter eas quaestiones, ob quas minime turbari aut scindi debeat Ecclesia, auctore Calvino l. 4. inst. cap. 1. §. 12. praesertim si in eo consensus sit, quod animae patrum veterum statim ab excessu beatitudine ac benefica Dei praesentia potirentur. Theophilus Antiochenus inter antiquos lib. 4. Alleg. In his quoque, ait, quod apud infernum Abrahamum videt, haec subesse a quibusdam ratio putatur, quod omnes sancti ante adventum Domini Jesu Christi etiam ad inferna, licet in refrigerii locum, descendisse dicuntur. Sic Jo. Chrysostomus hom. 4. in Marcum, Hieronymus ad Heliodorum in epitaphio Nepotiani, item ad Paulam super obitu Blesillae & ad Ecclesiasten cap. 3. & 9. Augustinus lib. 20. de C.D. cap. 15. & ep. 99. ad Evodium, Concilium Toletanum sub Honorio anno 633. celebratum, cap. 1. Descendit, inquit, ad inferos, ut sanctos, qui ibidem tenebantur, erueret: quam sententiam clare item asserunt Irenaeus, Tertullianus, Origenes, Gregorius Neocaesariensis, Eusebius, Macarius Hierosolymitanus, Basilius, Athanasius, Epiphanius, Cyrillus Hieros., Ambrosius, Rufinus, Synesius, imo & e junioribus Zwinglius in epist. ad Heb. 11.39.40. Calvinus in psychopannychia, Bullingerus ad Luc. 16.23. & Heb. 9.8. & 1.Pet. 3.19. & Martyr ad 2.Reg. 2.13.
